528.n: epic gen. νηός (Attic νεώς); accent from enclitic τε

529.n: from epic ἕταρος; genitive with ἀπονόσφι

529.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

530.n: in tmesis with φῦ (ἐμφύω 'grow into, cling to'); accent from enclitic τʼ; the line = 2.302, 11.247
= τε; τε … τε … τε links the three verbs
in tmesis: ἐν … φῦ = ἐνέφυ; unaugmented root aorist 'grew into'
in tmesis with ὀνόμαζε (ἐξονομάζω); accent from enclitic τʼ

531.n: athematic aorist ἐπτάμην; some manuscripts ἤλυθε (Monro's critical note on 15.531)
a bird on the right is a good omen

532.n: root aorist, of what happens at the moment of speaking (Monro on 15.532)

532.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

532.n: from the root of Latin avis 'bird', with a rare suffix of apparently enlarging sense, as υἱωνός 'grandson' (Monro on 15.532); predicate with ἐόντα

532.p: verb · pres. part. act. acc. sg. masc.
532.n: epic ἐών = ὤν; participle with ἔγνων: 'knew that it was'

533.n: genitive of comparison with βασιλεύτερον: 'than your (race)'

the reading of a corrector of one manuscript; most have the genitive γένευς, some γένεος, with ὑμετέρου; the contraction of a genitive in -εος is extremely rare in Homer (Monro's critical note on 15.533)
comparative formed from the noun βασιλεύς: 'more of a king', as Iliad 9.160

534.n: Telemachus and his house; ἐστέ understood
'powerful', in rule, as κρατέω 'bear rule', though the word is generally used of physical strength (Monro on 15.534)

535.p: verb · pf. part. mid./pass. nom. sg. masc.
535.n: perfect participle used as adjective 'wise, sensible'

536.n: αἲ γάρ + optative: a wish, 'would that'; epic αἰ = εἰ; 536–538 again 17.163–165, 19.309–311

536.p: verb · pf. part. pass. nom. sg. neut.

537.n: 'therefore, in that case', the dative of ὁ used adverbially
φιλότητά τε πολλά τε δῶρα, perhaps a hendiadys: hospitality shown in many gifts (Monro on 15.537); second accent from enclitic τε

538.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.

538.n: 'call happy' (μάκαρ); in Homer only here and in the repeated lines 17.165, 19.311

539.n: son of Clytius (540), Telemachus' companion on the voyage to Pylos (541); again 17.55, 20.372

540.n: patronymic: Peiraeus' father Clytius, whose house is named at 16.327
δέ after the address; accent from enclitic μοι
τά περ ἄλλα 'in all else', accusative of respect, as τά τʼ ἄλλα περ 5.29

541.n: partitive with σύ (540) and μάλιστα: 'most of my companions'
accusative of the goal, with εἰς placed after it

542.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
542.n: 'leading'; the infinitives of 543 act as imperatives
with ἄγων: take him and keep him in, a pregnant use

543.n: uncontracted (= φιλεῖν); infinitive for imperative: 'treat as a friend, entertain'
epic infinitive -έμεν (= τίειν); infinitive for imperative
εἰς ὅ 'up to the time when'

545.n: εἴ κεν with the optative: a condition put as possible (Monro on 15.545)
γάρ as a kind of interjection: 'why, if …' (Monro on 15.545)
Telemachus has landed not far from Eumaeus' homestead (Monro on 15.545)
printed μίμνοι; σύ requires the second person μίμνοις, which Monro prints

546.n: = τε, in the main clause after εἰ (545); so Wolf and Ludwich; Herodian read τόνδε δʼ (Monro's critical note on 15.546)
contracted future (= κομιέω): 'take care of'; the form only here in Homer
neuter plural as noun, 'the entertainment of a guest', as 514; three manuscripts ξεινίων (Monro's critical note on 15.546)
dative of possession: 'he shall have no lack'

547.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
547.n: Peiraeus, who now takes command of the ship and carries out Telemachus' orders of 503 (Monro on 15.547)

548.n: apocope: ἀμ- = ἀνα- before β; the embarking is put first as the main action, though the cables must have been loosed before (Monro on 15.548)
in tmesis with λῦσαι (ἀναλύω 'loose'); acute before enclitic τε
mooring cables from stern to shore

550.n: in tmesis with ὑπό; middle 'bound on himself'; the half-line as 1.96, 5.44

551.n: middle 'took for himself'; the line = 1.99, Iliad 10.135, 14.12, 15.482; his own spear (2.10), which would also be on the deck, not Theoclymenus' (283), as Ameis supposed (Monro on 15.551)
perfect participle in form (ἀκή 'point'): 'sharpened, tipped'; not ἀκαχίζω 'grieve'

552.n: = ἀπό; four manuscripts ἐπʼ (Monro's critical note on 15.552)
epic -φι(ν) ending, here as genitive with ἀπό: the half-deck at the stern
= πρυμνήσια; mooring cables from stern to shore; the half-line as 2.418

553.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. pl. masc.
553.n: 'pushing off': ἀνά 'out to sea', not of the direction of the voyage (Monro on 15.553); in Homer only here
unaugmented, uncontracted (= ἔπλεον); not the comparative πλέον 'more'

554.n: epic gen. -οιο; Ὀδυσσῆος θείοιο 'divine Odysseus', as Iliad 2.335

555.p: verb · pres. part. act. acc. sg. masc.
555.n: 'striding forward'; Aristarchus' form, as from βίβημι (βιβάς, βιβάντος); the manuscripts προβιβῶντα, the form of Iliad 13.807, which Monro would banish from Homer (Monro on 15.555 and his critical note)
the walled yard of the swineherd's steading, as 14.5; accusative of the goal

556.n: by-form ὗς (= σῦς); feminine, the sows, with μυρίαι
epic dat. pl. -ῃσι: the swine; dative with ἐνίαυεν (557)

557.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

557.n: 'passed the nights among' (ἐν + ἰαύω), + dat. ᾗσι (556); unaugmented; in Homer only here and 9.187
dat. pl. -εσι(ν) (Attic ἄναξι): Odysseus and his house; dative with ἤπια εἰδώς
ἤπια εἰδέναι 'be kindly disposed' (lit. 'know kind things'), + dat., as 13.405 (= 15.39)

557.p: verb · pf. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
